briefs.heading: Should the uploads disk be grown, or should uploads older than 90 days move to archive storage?
briefs.why_now: the disk has 90 GB free and takes about 38 GB each month; until you answer, nothing is changed and the disk fills in about two to three months
context: The uploads disk holds 500 GB and 410 GB of it is used (`docs/storage.md`).

Growing it takes the shop offline for about 30 minutes, and a disk that has grown never shrinks. The archive has no size limit but an upload opens in about 2 seconds from it, and in about 50 ms from the disk.
terms: storage with no size limit, slower to open, that a nightly job would fill with uploads older than 90 days
briefs.recommend: the archive lasts several times longer for any growth the log supports, and a move can be undone

options.leads_to: every upload stays on the disk, which lasts about 25 to 30 months at the growth in the log
options.choose_if: a fast open of every upload matters more than a nightly job to write and run
options.downside: the shop is offline for about 30 minutes, and the disk never shrinks again

options.leads_to: the disk holds the last three months, which lasts many years at the growth in the log
options.choose_if: lasting longest and keeping the choice open matter more than a fast open of an old upload
options.downside: an old upload opens in about 2 seconds, and nobody has measured how often that happens

briefs.not_checked: how often an upload older than 90 days is opened, which nobody has measured

undo.text: growing the disk cannot be undone; moving uploads to the archive is undone by moving them back
